intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of pressing, its prefixed form, the French noun of an impression, the English verb, and the endings that name the doer and the trade.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示压的拉丁语动词、加前缀的形式、法语中表示印记的名词、英语动词，以及命名做者与行当的词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere and its prefixed form imprimere stand at the head of this family, so the pressing image is recorded in Latin even though the modern trade word was shaped in French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 premere 及加前缀的 imprimere 处在这个词族的顶端，所以「压」的意象在拉丁语里就有记录，尽管现代行业词是在法语和英语里定型的。

items.meaning: one who or that which does
a person or machine that prints
the act or trade of printing

definition_zh: 先前的；更早的；优先的；更重要的；修道院院长；前科
definition_en: earlier in time or order, or higher in importance; also a monastic superior or a previous conviction
core_image: 排队时站在你前面的人，既更早到，也先被叫到
scene: 签约前，律师翻出旧协议。The lawyer opened the prior agreement before signing, to be sure the new clauses did not contradict the old ones.
sceneCN: 这里 prior 是「先前的、更早的」（第 1 个义项：在时间上更早）；句意：律师在签字前翻出先前的协议，确认新条款不会与旧约定冲突。图中可辨识物件：旧合同、新合同、日期页、文件夹、律师的眼镜；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 先前的；更早的；优先的；更重要的
修道院院长；前科（口语）

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

senses.title: Earlier in time
senses.definition: existing or happening before something else
senses.definitionCN: 比另一事物更早存在或发生
senses.example: She had prior experience in publishing.
senses.exampleCN: 她先前有出版经验。
senses.why: Latin prior is a comparative meaning 'former, first of two'. It compares two points on a line and names the one already passed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 prior 是比较级，意为“前者、两者中的第一个”。它比较线上的两点，命名已经过去的那一点。

senses.title: Preceding in order
senses.definition: coming before in a series or procedure
senses.definitionCN: 在系列或程序中出现得更早
senses.example: No changes may be made without prior approval.
senses.exampleCN: 未经事先批准不得改动。
senses.why: Procedures require gates: the prior step must be completed before the next begins. The word turns sequence into a condition.
senses.whyCN: 程序需要关口：前一步必须完成，下一步才能开始。这个词把次序变成条件。

senses.title: Higher in importance or rank
senses.definition: having a stronger claim or higher rank
senses.definitionCN: 拥有更强的请求权或更高的等级
senses.example: They have a prior claim on the land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这块土地有更优先的请求权。
senses.why: The Latin comparative could mean 'superior' as well as 'earlier'. Priority and precedence share the image of standing in front of the line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁比较级既可指“更早”，也可指“更优越”。优先与居先共享“站在队伍前面”的意象。

senses.title: Before, in the phrase prior to
senses.definition: in formal usage, before a time or event
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法：在某个时间或事件之前
senses.example: Prior to 2010, the firm had no overseas office.
senses.exampleCN: 2010 年之前，这家公司没有海外办事处。
senses.why: Prior to is the formal cousin of before. Legal and academic writing prefer it because it sounds procedural rather than conversational.
senses.whyCN: prior to 是 before 的正式表亲。法律与学术写作偏爱它，因为它听起来像程序而非口语。

senses.title: Presumed or existing earlier
senses.definition: in formal contexts, already held or existing before the present matter
senses.definitionCN: 正式语境中，在当前事项之前已持有或已存在
senses.example: The prior agreement still governs the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 先前的协议仍管辖这场争议。
senses.why: Law speaks of prior agreements, prior art, and prior rights: things that existed first and therefore constrain what can be done now.
senses.whyCN: 法律谈 prior agreements、prior art、prior rights：先已存在的事物，因此约束当下能做什么。

senses.title: A monastic superior
senses.definition: the head of a priory or a religious house
senses.definitionCN: 小修道院或宗教院舍的首脑
senses.example: The prior welcomed the visitors at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 院长在门口迎接访客。
senses.why: The noun came into English in the 14c. from Medieval Latin prior, 'superior'. The monastic prior stands first in his house, the same rank image as the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词 14 世纪从中世纪拉丁语 prior“上级”进入英语。修道院院长在其院舍中居首，与形容词的等级意象相同。

senses.title: A previous conviction (informal)
senses.definition: in informal legal usage, an earlier criminal conviction
senses.definitionCN: 非正式法律用语：先前的刑事定罪
senses.example: The defendant has two priors.
senses.exampleCN: 被告有两项前科。
senses.why: Police and court slang clip the phrase 'prior conviction' to priors. The word's temporal sense becomes a record that follows a person.
senses.whyCN: 警察与法庭俚语把 prior conviction 缩略为 priors。这个词的时间义变成一份跟随此人的记录。

senses.title: The antecedent in logic
senses.definition: in logic, the proposition from which another is inferred
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中推出另一命题所依据的前一命题
senses.example: If the prior is false, the conclusion fails.
senses.exampleCN: 如果前件为假，结论就不成立。
senses.why: Inference runs along a line: the prior proposition comes first and licenses the next. The temporal order becomes a relation of support.
senses.whyCN: 推理沿一条线运行：前件在先，并授权后件。时间次序变成支撑关系。

senses.title: Superior in rank (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, of higher rank or dignity
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：等级或尊严更高的
senses.example: the prior rank of a duke
senses.exampleCN: 公爵更高的等级
senses.why: This is the Latin comparative at full strength: prior as 'superior'. Modern English keeps the trace in the noun prior and in the idea of a prior claim.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁比较级的完整力量：prior 即“更优越”。现代英语在名词 prior 与“更优先的请求权”中留下痕迹。

intro.en: Prior entered English twice: first as a noun for a monastic superior, then as an adjective for 'earlier'. Both come from Latin prior, a comparative meaning 'former, first of two', which also gives priority and primacy.
intro.cn: prior 两次进入英语：先作名词指修道院院长，后作形容词指“更早”。两者都来自拉丁语 prior——一个意为“前者、两者中第一”的比较级，它也生成 priority 与 primacy。

items.en: The noun is first recorded for the superior of a priory or religious house, from Medieval Latin prior.
items.cn: 名词最早记录指小修道院或宗教院舍的上级，来自中世纪拉丁语 prior。

items.en: Latin prior 'former, previous, first of two' is a comparative of an old adjective *pri- 'before'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 prior“前者、先前的、两者中第一”是古形容词 *pri-“在前”的比较级。

items.en: The root is traced to PIE *per- 'before, first', also behind first, prime, and principal. The reconstruction is standard.
items.cn: 词根被追溯到原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”，也见于 first、prime、principal。该重构是通行说法。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English with the sense 'earlier, previous'.
items.cn: 形容词在英语中记录为“更早的、先前的”。

items.en: prior to becomes a formal preposition, and the legal phrase prior claim spreads.
items.cn: prior to 成为正式介词，法律短语 prior claim 传播开来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the religious noun and the temporal adjective side by side, plus the informal plural priors for convictions.
items.cn: 现代英语让宗教名词与时间形容词并存，另有口语复数 priors 指前科。

note.en: The first group shares the prior/priority stem; the second is about words that also mean earlier or more important.
note.cn: 第一组共享 prior/priority 词干，第二组看同样表示“更早”或“更重要”的词。

entries.definition: the state of being first in rank or the thing ranked first. It comes from Medieval Latin prioritas.
entries.definitionCN: 优先地位；优先事项。来自中世纪拉丁语 prioritas。

entries.definition: a small monastery headed by a prior.
entries.definitionCN: 由院长主持的小修道院。

entries.definition: a female superior of a priory.
entries.definitionCN: 女修道院院长。

entries.definition: earlier, especially the one just before. It is less formal than prior.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的，尤指刚过去的那一个。它比 prior 少些正式。

entries.definition: the earlier of two, or a past role-holder. It contrasts with latter.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中在前的，或前任。与 latter 相对。

entries.definition: coming immediately before in order. It is purely positional.
entries.definitionCN: 在次序上紧接其前。它纯粹是位置性的。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin prior as a comparative, the noun for a monastic superior, the phrase prior to, and the legal sense of a prior claim.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 prior 的比较级性质、指修道院院长的名词、短语 prior to，以及 prior claim 的法律义。

normal.en: Prior is a Latin comparative: it compares two things and names the earlier one.
normal.cn: prior 是拉丁比较级：它比较两物，并命名更早的那一个。

normal.en: The same comparative can mean 'superior', which is why prior also means 'more important'.
normal.cn: 同一比较级也可指“更优越”，所以 prior 也表“更重要”。

normal.en: The noun prior is a different borrowing: the head of a priory stands first in his house.
normal.cn: 名词 prior 是另一次借入：小修道院院长在其院舍中居首。

normal.en: Prior to is formal 'before'; lawyers and academics prefer it to sound procedural.
normal.cn: prior to 是正式的 before；律师与学者偏爱它，以显得程序化。

normal.en: In police slang, priors are prior convictions: the past that follows a person.
normal.cn: 警察俚语中，priors 是前科：跟随一个人的过去。

abstract.en: Time and rank collapse into one word: what came first is assumed to deserve first place.
abstract.cn: 时间与等级在此塌缩成一个词：先来的，被假定该先得。

abstract.en: A prior claim is a promise the past makes to the present.
abstract.cn: 优先请求权是过去对当下作出的承诺。

abstract.en: The comparative form is the point: prior never stands alone, it always implies a second term.
abstract.cn: 重点在比较级形式：prior 从不孤立，它总隐含另一个项。

examples.en: You need prior approval before changing the budget.
examples.cn: 改动预算前需要事先批准。

examples.en: Prior to joining the firm, she taught at a university.
examples.cn: 加入这家公司之前，她在大学任教。

examples.en: The court considered his prior convictions.
examples.cn: 法庭考虑了他的前科。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来尔”——先扑过来排队的那一个 → prior 先前的、优先的

root: 拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”，是 *pri-“在前”的比较级；更早为原始印欧语 *per-。同族有 priority、prime、principal。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of prior, all comparative. The word always implies a second term: this one is earlier, or higher, or both. It can point to a time, a rank, a right, a monastic office, or a criminal record.
sensesIntro.cn: prior 的九个义项都是比较性的。这个词总隐含另一个项：这一个更早，或更高，或两者兼有。它可以指时间、等级、权利、修道职务或犯罪记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the one standing earlier in the line, and therefore first in line.
core.cn: 核心意象：在队伍中站得更早、因而更靠前的那一个。

branches.en: TIME: an earlier point or step, including agreements already in force.
branches.cn: 时间：更早的时间点或步骤，包括已生效的协议。

branches.en: RANK: the comparative shades into superiority and precedence.
branches.cn: 等级：比较级滑向优越与居先。

branches.en: PREPOSITION: prior to is the formal 'before'.
branches.cn: 介词：prior to 是正式的“在……之前”。

branches.en: OFFICE: the monastic prior stands first in his house.
branches.cn: 职务：修道院院长在其院舍中居首。

branches.en: RECORD AND LOGIC: prior convictions, and the antecedent proposition.
branches.cn: 记录与逻辑：前科，以及逻辑前件。

intro.en: Prior is both adjective and noun. English adds -ity, -ize, and -y, and the Latin comparative also underlies priority and primacy.
intro.cn: prior 既是形容词也是名词。英语加 -ity、-ize、-y，拉丁比较级还支撑 priority 与 primacy。

latinIntro.en: Latin prior 'former, first of two' is a comparative beside primus 'first' and *pri- 'before'. Its noun prioritas gives English priority.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”是与 primus“第一”、*pri-“在前”相邻的比较级。其名词 prioritas 生成英语 priority。

items.meaning: first place in rank; a thing ranked first
items.meaningCN: 优先；优先事项（-ity 构成名词）

items.meaning: to treat as more important than others
items.meaningCN: 优先处理（-ize 构成动词）

items.meaning: the act of ranking things by importance
a monastery headed by a prior
the office or term of a prior

latinEntries.meaningCN: 前者；先前的；两者中第一

definition_zh: 优先；优先权；优先事项；优先次序；（计算机）优先级
definition_en: the state of being more important than something else, or a thing that is ranked first
core_image: 急诊分诊台上，红色标签的伤员先被推进手术室
scene: 医院分诊时，护士把红黄绿标签贴在病历夹上。The triage nurse set the priority of each patient by colour, so the most serious cases were seen first.
sceneCN: 这里 priority 是「优先次序、优先级」（第 3 个义项：按重要性排出的先后顺序）；句意：分诊护士用颜色给每位病人排定优先次序，最危重的先看。图中可辨识物件：分诊台、红黄绿标签、担架、病历夹、时钟；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 优先；优先权；优先事项；优先次序

derivatives.zh: 优先处理；按优先级排序

senses.title: The thing ranked first
senses.definition: the thing that is treated as most important
senses.definitionCN: 被当作最重要的事情
senses.example: Patient safety is our top priority.
senses.exampleCN: 病人安全是我们的头等大事。
senses.why: Priority is the noun of prior: it names whatever stands first in a line. In modern management, that first thing is often called a priority in the plural.
senses.whyCN: priority 是 prior 的名词：它命名排在队伍最前的东西。现代管理中，这个“第一之物”常用复数 priorities 表示。

senses.title: The state of being more important
senses.definition: the condition of having a stronger claim than others
senses.definitionCN: 拥有比其余更强的地位
senses.example: The issue has priority over all others.
senses.exampleCN: 这个议题优先于其余一切。
senses.why: The word can name a status rather than a thing: something has priority. It is a relation, not an object, and it always implies competitors.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以命名状态而非事物：某物具有 priority。它是一种关系，不是物件，而且总隐含竞争者。

senses.title: An order of precedence
senses.definition: a ranking that decides what is handled first
senses.definitionCN: 决定先处理什么的排序
senses.example: The committee set its priorities for the year.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会定下了年度优先次序。
senses.why: Once several items compete, priority becomes a list. The plural is natural here: a set of ranked claims, not one favourite.
senses.whyCN: 一旦多项事务竞争，priority 就变成一份列表。复数在此很自然：一组被排序的诉求，而非一个宠儿。

senses.title: The right to go first
senses.definition: the right of a vehicle or person to move before others
senses.definitionCN: 车辆或人先于他人行动的权利
senses.example: Bicycles have priority at this crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 自行车在这个路口有优先通行权。
senses.why: Traffic rules codify the line: priority marks who may move first. The metaphor becomes legal and physical at the same time.
senses.whyCN: 交通规则把队伍编码：priority 标记谁可以先动。这个隐喻同时变成法律与物理的。

senses.title: Ceremonial precedence
senses.definition: the rank order of people at a formal occasion
senses.definitionCN: 正式场合中人们的位次顺序
senses.example: The ambassador's priority in the procession was fixed.
senses.exampleCN: 大使在行列中的位次是固定的。
senses.why: Court and diplomacy rank bodies in space: who enters first, who sits nearest. Priority is the abstract name for that spatial order.
senses.whyCN: 宫廷与外交按空间给人排序：谁先进、谁坐得最近。priority 是那种空间秩序的抽象名称。

senses.title: A computing priority level
senses.definition: a value that decides how soon a task is serviced
senses.definitionCN: 决定任务多快被处理的一个值
senses.example: The process runs at high priority.
senses.exampleCN: 这个进程以高优先级运行。
senses.why: Operating systems borrow the queue image: every task waits, and priority decides who jumps ahead. It is the same ranking, made numeric.
senses.whyCN: 操作系统借用排队意象：每个任务都在等，优先级决定谁插到前面。还是同一个排序，只是变成数字。

senses.title: Top priority
senses.definition: the single most urgent item, in the phrase top priority
senses.definitionCN: 短语 top priority：唯一最紧迫的事项
senses.example: Rebuilding the bridge is a top priority.
senses.exampleCN: 重建桥梁是首要任务。
senses.why: Top priority doubles the ranking: top already means first, priority already means first. The redundancy marks urgency, which is why it is so common in politics.
senses.whyCN: top priority 重复了排序：top 已是第一，priority 已是第一。这种冗余标记紧迫性，所以它在政治语言中如此常见。

senses.title: Low priority
senses.definition: an item that can wait, in the phrase low priority
senses.definitionCN: 短语 low priority：可以等待的事项
senses.example: The paint job is a low priority this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年粉刷是次要事项。
senses.why: The scale runs from top to low. Low priority is not unimportant but postponable: the item stays in the queue, just further back.
senses.whyCN: 这个尺度从 top 到 low。low priority 不是不重要，而是可推迟：事项仍在队列里，只是更靠后。

senses.title: Earlier status in time (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, the state of being earlier in time
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：在时间上更早的状态
senses.example: The priority of the claim depended on its date.
senses.exampleCN: 这项权利的在先性取决于它的日期。
senses.why: The oldest sense was temporal: priority meant being earlier. Modern English keeps the temporal trace mainly in law, where an earlier filing wins.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是时间性的：priority 指更早。现代英语主要在法律中保留时间痕迹：先提交者胜。

intro.en: Priority is the noun of prior, formed in Medieval Latin as prioritas. It began as 'the state of being earlier' and grew into 'the right to be first', which is why both time and rank live inside it.
intro.cn: priority 是 prior 的名词，在中世纪拉丁语中作 prioritas。它始于“更早的状态”，发展为“居先的权利”，所以时间与等级都住在它里面。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'the state of being earlier or prior'.
items.cn: 最早在英语中记录为“更早或在先的状态”。

items.en: From prioritas 'priority, precedence', from Latin prior 'former, first of two'.
items.cn: 来自中世纪拉丁语 prioritas“优先、居先”，源出拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”。

items.en: prior is a comparative of *pri- 'before', from PIE *per- 'before, first'.
items.cn: prior 是 *pri-“在前”的比较级，更早为原始印欧语 *per-“在前、第一”。

items.en: The sense widens from temporal precedence to rank and ceremonial order.
items.cn: 义项从时间上的在先扩展到等级与礼仪次序。

items.en: Management and administration make priority a countable item: priorities are things to be ranked.
items.cn: 管理与行政把 priority 变成可数事项：priorities 是待排序的东西。

items.en: Modern English also uses priority in computing, traffic law, and diplomacy, wherever a queue needs a rule.
items.cn: 现代英语还把 priority 用于计算机、交通法与外交，凡队列需要规则之处皆可。

note.en: The first group shares the prior stem; the second is about words that also mean precedence or importance.
note.cn: 第一组共享 prior 词干，第二组看同样表示“居先”或“重要”的词。

entries.definition: earlier or more important. It is the adjective behind priority.
entries.definitionCN: 更早或更重要的。它是 priority 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: to rank things and act on the first one.
entries.definitionCN: 排序并先处理第一项。

entries.definition: the act of ranking by importance.
entries.definitionCN: 按重要性排序的行为。

entries.definition: the right to go before others, especially in ceremony. It stresses order, not urgency.
entries.definitionCN: 先于他人的权利，尤用于礼仪。它强调次序，而非紧迫。

entries.definition: a liking for one thing over another. It is personal taste, not a ranked obligation.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物胜过另一物的喜爱。它是个人偏好，不是排序义务。

entries.definition: the quality of needing immediate action. It explains why something is a priority.
entries.definitionCN: 需要立即行动的性质。它解释某事为何成为优先。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Medieval Latin prioritas, the prior/priority pair, triage and traffic uses, and the phrases top priority and low priority.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：中世纪拉丁语 prioritas、prior 与 priority 这对词、分诊与交通用法，以及 top priority / low priority 两个短语。

normal.en: Priority is prior plus -ity: it names whatever stands first in the line.
normal.cn: priority 是 prior 加 -ity：它命名排在队伍最前的东西。

normal.en: It can be a thing (a priority) or a status (to have priority). The first is countable, the second is relational.
normal.cn: 它可以是事物（a priority），也可以是状态（to have priority）。前者可数，后者是关系。

normal.en: Triage is priority in action: red tags move first, green tags wait.
normal.cn: 分诊是 priority 的实战：红标先走，绿标等待。

normal.en: Top priority is deliberately redundant; the doubling signals urgency in political speech.
normal.cn: top priority 是刻意冗余；这种重复在政治语言中标记紧迫。

normal.en: Low priority does not mean unimportant: it means postponable, still in the queue.
normal.cn: low priority 不是不重要：它意味着可推迟，仍在队列里。

abstract.en: Priority is scarcity made visible: when time or space is limited, someone must be ranked above someone else.
abstract.cn: 优先是稀缺的可见化：当时间或空间有限，总得有人被排在别人之上。

abstract.en: Every ranking is an argument about values disguised as a schedule.
abstract.cn: 每一种排序都是伪装成日程的价值争论。

abstract.en: The word began as 'earlier' and became 'more important'; modern life quietly assumes the first deserves the second.
abstract.cn: 这个词从“更早”变成“更重要”；现代生活悄悄假定先来的理应优先。

examples.en: The safety of children must take priority over cost.
examples.cn: 儿童安全必须优先于成本。

examples.en: Deciding priorities is the hardest part of the job.
examples.cn: 决定优先次序是这份工作最难的部分。

examples.en: Emergency vehicles have priority at the junction.
examples.cn: 紧急车辆在交叉口有优先通行权。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑来奥瑞提”——先扑过来的那一个，奥瑞提先被叫号 → priority 优先、优先事项

root: 中世纪拉丁语 prioritas“优先、居先”，源出拉丁语 prior“前者、两者中第一”，再上为 *pri- / PIE *per-“在前”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of priority, all about a queue. The queue can be moral (top priority), legal (the right of way), ceremonial (order of procession), or digital (a process level).
sensesIntro.cn: priority 的九个义项都关于一条队列。这条队列可以是道德的（头等大事）、法律的（通行权）、礼仪的（行列位次）或数字的（进程等级）。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ranked queue in which one item is served first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被排序的队列，其中一项先被服务。

branches.en: FIRST CLAIM: one thing is treated as more important, whether named or as a status.
branches.cn: 第一诉求：某物被当作更重要，无论作为事项还是状态。

branches.en: ORDER: several claims are ranked into a list or a ceremonial sequence.
branches.cn: 次序：多项诉求被排成列表或礼仪序列。

branches.en: TRAFFIC: the ranking becomes a right to move first.
branches.cn: 交通：排序变成先行动的权利。

branches.en: COMPUTING: the queue is numeric, and priority decides which task jumps ahead.
branches.cn: 计算机：队列变成数字，优先级决定哪个任务插队。

branches.en: SCALE AND TIME: top and low mark urgency, while the archaic sense keeps the temporal origin.
branches.cn: 尺度与时间：top 与 low 标记紧迫，古义保留时间起源。

intro.en: Priority is a noun from Medieval Latin prioritas. English adds -ize, -ation, and -ed, and the base prior also gives priory and prioress.
intro.cn: priority 是来自中世纪拉丁 prioritas 的名词。英语加 -ize、-ation、-ed，词基 prior 还生成 priory 与 prioress。

latinIntro.en: Latin prior 'former' and prioritas 'precedence' sit beside primus 'first'. The family ranks things along a line from earlier to more important.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 prior“前者”与 prioritas“居先”旁边是 primus“第一”。这个词族沿一条从“更早”到“更重要”的线给事物排序。

items.meaning: to treat one thing as more important than others
items.meaningCN: 优先处理（-ize 构成动词）

items.meaning: the act of ranking by importance
ranked and treated as most important
a monastery headed by a prior
a female superior of a priory

items.meaningCN: 居先；位次优先（近义同族）

definition_zh: 隐私；不受他人打扰的状态，以及对个人信息的控制权
definition_en: the state of being free from public attention or disturbance, and the control a person has over personal information
core_image: 一间只亮着一盏灯的屋子，窗帘拉严，门外的人只能看见布上的影子，却进不来
scene: 深夜的屋子里只亮着一盏台灯，窗帘拉得很严，门外的人只能看见布上的影子。She drew the curtain because privacy mattered more to her than the view.
sceneCN: 这里 privacy 指不受他人注视与打扰的状态（第 1 个义项：独处不受扰）；句意：她拉上窗帘，因为对她来说，不被打扰比窗外的景色更重要。

pos.zh: 隐私；私生活；独处不受扰；信息控制权

senses.title: Freedom from being disturbed
senses.definition: the condition of being alone and free from other people's interruption
senses.definitionCN: 独处且不被他人打断的状态
senses.example: He reads in the garden for an hour of privacy each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上在花园里读一小时书，享受不被打扰的时光。
senses.why: the Latin adjective described something withdrawn from public life, and withdrawal begins as simple freedom from company.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词指从公共生活中退开，而退开最初就是免于他人陪伴。

senses.title: Freedom from public attention
senses.definition: the state of not being watched, reported on or discussed by the public
senses.definitionCN: 不被公众注视、报道或议论的状态
senses.example: The family moved inland to raise the children in privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人搬到内陆，想在不受注视的环境里抚养孩子。
senses.why: publicity is the opposite pole, and the word names the absence of it rather than the presence of walls.
senses.whyCN: 「公开」是对立的一端，这个词指公开的缺席，而不是墙的存在。

senses.title: Control over one's own information
senses.definition: a person's power to decide who learns what about them
senses.definitionCN: 个人决定谁能知道自己哪些情况的权力
senses.example: Privacy means the choice to tell, not the duty to hide.
senses.exampleCN: 隐私意味着「可以选择说」，而不是「必须藏」。
senses.why: once information could be copied and shared at scale, withdrawal became a matter of control rather than of distance.
senses.whyCN: 当信息能被大规模复制与共享，退开就从「隔开距离」变成了「掌握控制权」。

senses.title: Data privacy as a field of practice
senses.titleCN: 数据隐私这一实务领域
senses.definition: the handling of personal data by organisations under rules of collection, use and deletion
senses.definitionCN: 机构按收集、使用与删除规则处理个人数据
senses.example: The company hired a lawyer to lead its data privacy work.
senses.exampleCN: 公司聘请了一位律师主管数据隐私工作。
senses.why: a social value is turned into a managed operation, and its name follows the operation.
senses.whyCN: 一项社会价值被转化为可管理的业务，其名称便随业务走。

senses.title: The legal right to seclusion
senses.definition: the recognised claim that others may not intrude into one's personal sphere
senses.definitionCN: 被承认的、他人不得侵入个人领域的主张
senses.example: The court treated privacy as a limit on how evidence may be gathered.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把隐私视为取证方式的一条界限。
senses.why: a value argued in courts becomes a right, and the abstract noun carries that legal weight.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上被论证的价值会变成一项权利，这个抽象名词便承担了法律分量。

senses.title: Settings that limit visibility
senses.definition: the options in an app or account that decide who can see what
senses.definitionCN: 应用或账号中决定谁能看到什么的选择项
senses.example: She changed her privacy so that only friends could see the album.
senses.exampleCN: 她改动了隐私设置，只有好友能看到那本相册。
senses.why: when exposure is governed by menus, the value word is used for the switches themselves.
senses.whyCN: 当曝光由菜单控制时，这个价值名词就被用来指那些开关。

senses.title: Confidentiality of a matter
senses.definition: the quality of a discussion or document that stays within a trusted circle
senses.definitionCN: 谈话或文件只留在可信圈子内的性质
senses.example: They asked for privacy during the settlement talks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们要求和解谈判过程保持保密。
senses.why: a thing kept from outsiders is private in the old sense, and the abstract noun covers that condition.
senses.whyCN: 不让外人知道的事在旧义上就是「私下的」，抽象名词涵盖这种状态。

senses.title: Physical seclusion of a place
senses.definition: the shielding of a room or home from view, sound or entry
senses.definitionCN: 房间或住宅在视线、声音与进入上受到的遮蔽
senses.example: The hedge gives the terrace a little privacy from the road.
senses.exampleCN: 那道树篱让露台与马路之间有了一点遮蔽。
senses.why: walls, hedges and curtains are the oldest tools of withdrawal, so the word attaches to physical shelter.
senses.whyCN: 墙、树篱与窗帘是「退开」最古老的工具，因此这个词也依附于实体的遮蔽。

senses.title: Protection against surveillance
senses.definition: the expectation that states and companies will not track a person without cause
senses.definitionCN: 国家对个人的追踪需有正当理由这一期待
senses.example: Cameras on every corner turned privacy into a public argument.
senses.exampleCN: 街角的摄像头把隐私变成了公共议题。
senses.why: the word sharpens when watching becomes cheap, because the old freedom now needs defending.
senses.whyCN: 当「观看」变得廉价，这个词就变得尖锐，因为旧的自由如今需要辩护。

senses.title: Personal space in shared settings
senses.titleCN: 共享场所中的个人空间
senses.definition: the informal room a person keeps around themselves among others
senses.definitionCN: 在他人之间为自己留出的非正式余地
senses.example: Open desks leave almost no privacy for a phone call.
senses.exampleCN: 开放式工位几乎不给人打电话的私人余地。
senses.why: the word stretches from legal seclusion to the small distance people maintain in a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法律的清静延伸到人群中人们维持的那点距离。

intro.en: Privacy comes from Latin privatus, withdrawn from public office and belonging to oneself. The abstract ending -acy names a state, so the word names a condition rather than a thing.
intro.cn: privacy 来自拉丁语 privatus，指「退出公职、属于个人」。抽象词尾 -acy 表示状态，因此这个词指一种处境，而不是一件东西。

items.en: Latin privus meant single, each for itself, and the derived verb privare meant to set apart or deprive.
items.cn: 拉丁语 privus 意为「单个的、各自的」，派生动词 privare 意为「分开、剥夺」。

items.en: Privatus described a person withdrawn from public office, a private citizen as opposed to a magistrate.
items.cn: privatus 描述退出公职的人，即与官员相对的普通公民。

items.en: French privé carried the sense of personal or secluded, and English borrowed the adjective as private.
items.cn: 法语 privé 带有「个人的、僻静的」之意，英语借入形容词 private。

items.en: The ending -acy, from Latin -acia, turns an adjective into the name of a state, so privacy is the state of being private.
items.cn: 词尾 -acy 来自拉丁 -acia，把形容词变成状态之名，因此 privacy 就是「处于私人状态」。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word moved from seclusion to information, as records became easy to copy and share.
items.cn: 二十世纪，随着记录变得易于复制与共享，这个词从「清静」转向「信息」。

items.en: Source uncertain: the link between privus and the wider family of Latin separating words is debated, and the deeper forms are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：privus 与拉丁语中其他表示「分开」的词是否同源仍有争论，更古的形式属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is built on the same private root; the second group is the neighbouring ideas of secrecy, solitude and protection.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「私人」词根上；第二组是保密、独处与保护这些相邻概念。

entries.definition: Belonging to a person rather than the public; a private room is the place where privacy is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 属于个人而非公众；private 的房间就是能有 privacy 的地方。

entries.definition: In a way that avoids public view; it describes how something is done, not the state itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以避开公众视线的方式；它描述做事方式，而不是状态本身。

entries.definition: To take something away from someone; it comes from the same Latin verb of setting apart but means loss, not seclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从某人处拿走；出自同一个表示「分开」的拉丁动词，但指失去，不是清静。

entries.definition: A special right granted to a person or group; the root idea of a private law applied to one party survives here.
entries.definitionCN: 授予个人或群体的特殊权利；这里保留的是「针对一方的私人法规」这一词根含义。

entries.definition: The keeping of information from others; privacy protects a person's sphere, secrecy hides a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 把信息瞒住；privacy 保护个人领域，secrecy 隐藏某个事实。

entries.definition: The state of being alone, often chosen for calm; privacy can be enjoyed in company by being left undisturbed.
entries.definitionCN: 独处的状态，常为求安宁而选择；privacy 也可以在人群中通过不被打扰而获得。

entries.definition: The obligation not to pass on information given in trust; it is a duty, while privacy is a condition or right.
entries.definitionCN: 不转述受托信息的义务；它是义务，而 privacy 是状态或权利。

entries.definition: The state of not being identified; privacy may keep a known person unobserved, anonymity removes the name itself.
entries.definitionCN: 不被识别的状态；privacy 可让已知的人不被注视，anonymity 则连名字都去掉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations from the real Latin root and the real legal and technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：来自真实拉丁词根与真实的法律、技术搭配。

normal.en: The adjective is private and the state is privacy: the ending -acy names a condition.
normal.cn: 形容词是 private，状态名词是 privacy：词尾 -acy 表示状态。

normal.en: The old sense is a private citizen withdrawn from office, not a secret kept from a friend.
normal.cn: 旧义是退出公职的普通公民，而不是对朋友隐瞒的秘密。

normal.en: Fixed phrases run from law to software: right to privacy, privacy policy, privacy settings.
normal.cn: 固定搭配从法律延伸到软件：隐私权、隐私政策、隐私设置。

normal.en: The verb is invade or protect: privacy is something done to, not something done.
normal.cn: 动词是 invade 或 protect：privacy 是被对待的对象，而不是动作。

normal.en: Data privacy is the modern centre of gravity of the word.
normal.cn: 数据隐私是这个词现代的重心所在。

abstract.en: Picture a lit room whose curtain lets light out but keeps eyes out.
abstract.cn: 想象一间亮灯的屋子，窗帘把光放出去，却把目光挡在外面。

abstract.en: Picture a door with no handle on the outside and no lock on the inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，外面没有把手，里面没有锁。

abstract.en: Picture a name written in water and read only by the person who wrote it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个写在水上的名字，只有写下它的人读得到。

examples.en: Privacy is not secrecy; it is the power to decide what is shared.
examples.cn: 隐私不是保密，而是决定分享什么的权力。

examples.en: The new rules give patients more privacy over their records.
examples.cn: 新规让患者对自己的病历拥有更多隐私掌控。

examples.en: A thin wall gave the neighbours almost no privacy.
examples.cn: 一堵薄墙几乎没给邻居留下任何私人空间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来（pri）为谁（vacy）」——扑过来想知道「为谁」，正是要守住隐私

root: 拉丁 privus「单个的、各自的」→ privare「分开、剥夺」→ privatus「退出公职的私人」→ 法语 privé → 英语 private；加 -acy（拉丁 -acia）表状态构成 privacy。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses start from being left alone, pass through public attention, information control, professional handling, legal right, app settings, confidentiality and physical shelter, and end at surveillance and shared space.
sensesIntro.cn: 十个义项从「不被打扰」出发，经过公众注视、信息控制、行业实务、法律权利、应用设置、保密与实体遮蔽，最后落在监控与共享空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit room sealed by a curtain, visible as a glow from outside but not open to eyes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间亮灯的屋子被窗帘封住，外面只看见光，却看不进去。

branches.en: QUIET AND SHELTER: being undisturbed, and the walls or hedges that make it possible.
branches.cn: 清静与遮蔽：不被打扰，以及使之成为可能的墙与树篱。

branches.en: PUBLICITY AND WATCHING: the absence of public notice, and the defence of that absence against surveillance.
branches.cn: 公开与注视：不受公众关注，以及针对监控为这种缺席辩护。

branches.en: INFORMATION CONTROL: deciding who may know what about oneself.
branches.cn: 信息控制：决定谁能知道自己哪些情况。

branches.en: ROUTINE AND SETTINGS: organisational data handling, and the switches that govern visibility.
branches.cn: 实务与设置：机构的数据处理，以及控制可见性的开关。

branches.en: RIGHT, CONFIDENCE, SPACE: a legal claim, a confidential circle, and the small room kept in a crowd.
branches.cn: 权利、信任与空间：法律主张、可信圈子，以及在人群中留出的余地。

intro.en: Privacy is a Latin adjective turned into a state noun by the ending -acy; English later built private and privately from the same base.
intro.cn: privacy 是拉丁形容词加 -acy 构成的状态名词；英语后来又从同一词基造出 private 与 privately。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is privus, single or separate, with privatus as its adjective of withdrawal; -acia supplied the abstract ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 privus「单个的、分开的」，其形容词 privatus 表示退出；抽象词尾来自 -acia。

items.example: The adjective begins the idea of what belongs to one person.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词开启了「属于一个人」的观念。

items.example: The verb supplies both the sense of separation and of loss.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词同时提供「分开」与「失去」两层含义。

items.example: The adjective describes a private citizen rather than a magistrate.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述普通公民而非官员。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective into the name of a condition.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词变成状态之名。

items.example: Private is the adjective behind the state noun.
items.exampleCN: private 是状态名词背后的形容词。

items.example: The adverb describes the manner of doing something.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词描述做某事的方式。

items.example: The prefixed verb names loss rather than seclusion.
items.exampleCN: 带前缀的动词指失去，而不是清静。

items.example: The same base appears in a word for a special right.
items.exampleCN: 同一词基也出现在表示特殊权利的词中。

items.example: The second element ties the word to a private law.
items.exampleCN: 第二个构件把这个词与「私人法规」联系起来。

definition_en: belonging to one person or a small group rather than to the public; kept secret from others; not run by the state; free from other people; and, as a noun, a soldier of the lowest rank

senses.title: Belonging to one person rather than to the public
senses.definition: owned by or intended for one person or a small group, not for everyone
senses.definitionCN: 属于或专供一个人、一小群人，而不是给所有人的
senses.example: The letters are part of his private collection.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件是他私人收藏的一部分。
senses.why: Latin privus meant single or individual, the direct opposite of publicus, so the first sense is ownership narrowed down to one person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 privus 意为单个的、个人的，正好与 publicus 相对；所以第一层意思就是把归属缩到一个人身上。

senses.title: Kept from the knowledge of others
senses.definition: shared with only a few people and deliberately kept away from the public
senses.definitionCN: 只在少数人之间分享、有意不让公众知道的
senses.example: The meeting was private, so no notes were published.
senses.exampleCN: 那场会是不公开的，所以没有公布记录。
senses.why: What belongs to one person is also what only that person may know, so the ownership sense slides naturally into secrecy.
senses.whyCN: 属于一个人的东西，也就是只许那个人知道的东西，于是「归属」这一层自然而然地滑向「保密」。

senses.title: Not run or paid for by the state
senses.definition: owned and managed by an individual or a company rather than by the government
senses.definitionCN: 由个人或公司拥有经营，而不是由政府办的
senses.example: She moved her son from a state school to a private one.
senses.exampleCN: 她把儿子从公立学校转到了私立学校。
senses.why: When the state became the default provider of schools and hospitals, anything outside it was marked with the old word for what belongs to an individual, and this institutional sense followed.
senses.whyCN: 当国家成为学校和医院的默认提供者，凡是国家之外的就用那个表示「属于个人」的旧词来标记，这一层机构义便随之出现。

senses.title: Quiet and free from other people
senses.definition: away from crowds and public view, so that a person is not observed
senses.definitionCN: 远离人群和公众视线，人不被旁人看到
senses.example: The garden is private, and no visitors are allowed inside.
senses.exampleCN: 那座花园是私家的，访客不得入内。
senses.why: A place can be private too: if it belongs to one household, outsiders stay out, and the result is the quiet of a spot no one else enters.
senses.whyCN: 地方也可以是 private：它属于一户人家，外人就不进来，结果就是一处没人进入的安静之地。

senses.title: A soldier of the lowest rank
senses.definition: a soldier of the lowest rank, especially in the British army
senses.definitionCN: 最低军衔的士兵，尤指英国陆军中的
senses.example: He joined up as a private and retired as a sergeant.
senses.exampleCN: 他入伍时是列兵，退役时已是中士。
senses.why: The noun began as private soldier, a man serving in his own private capacity rather than as an officer, and the shorter form kept only the rank.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词起初写作 private soldier，指以个人身份服役、而非军官的人；后来缩写只留下了军衔这一层。

intro.en: Private comes from a Latin adjective meaning single or set apart, and its family keeps two faces: what belongs to one person, and what has been cut off from the rest.
intro.cn: private 出自一个意为「单个的、被分出来的」拉丁语形容词，它的词族始终保留两张面孔：属于一个人的，以及从其余部分中割出来的。

items.en: Privus meant single, individual or set apart, and it stood opposite publicus, what belongs to the people as a whole.
items.cn: privus 意为单个的、个人的、被单独分出来的，与表示「属于全体人民的」publicus 相对。

items.en: The verb privare meant to set apart or to deprive, and it supplied the idea of taking something away from the group.
items.cn: 动词 privare 意为使分离、剥夺，给出「把某物从群体中拿走」这一层意思。

items.en: Its participle privatus described a person withdrawn from public office, and from that came the sense of personal rather than official.
items.cn: 它的分词 privatus 形容退离公职的人，由此生出「属于个人而非公职」的意思。

items.en: Old French privat meant private, intimate and secret, and Middle English borrowed the word with that whole spread of meaning.
items.cn: 古法语 privat 意为私人的、亲近的、秘密的，中古英语把这一整片含义一起借了过来。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective for ownership, secrecy, non-state services and quiet places, while private soldier was shortened to private for the lowest rank.
items.cn: 现代英语保留形容词的四种用法：归属、保密、非国营与僻静；private soldier 则缩成 private，指最低军衔。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem priv- and the words English built on it; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives about what belongs to one person or is kept hidden.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁词干 priv- 及英语在它上面造出的词展开；近义组收表示「属于一个人」或「被藏起来」的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being free from public attention; built on the same stem with -acy.
entries.definitionCN: 不受公众注意的状态；同一词干加 -acy 构成。

entries.definition: In a private way, not publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 以私下的方式，非公开地。

entries.definition: The state of lacking something necessary; from Latin privatio.
entries.definitionCN: 缺少必需之物的状态；来自拉丁语 privatio。

entries.definition: To take something away from someone; built on the same Latin verb privare.
entries.definitionCN: 从某人那里拿走某物；建立在同一个拉丁动词 privare 上。

entries.definition: Relating to one particular person rather than to others.
entries.definitionCN: 与某一个特定的人有关，而非与其他人有关。

entries.definition: Kept hidden from other people.
entries.definitionCN: 对其他的人隐藏起来的。

entries.definition: Meant to be kept private between a few people.
entries.definitionCN: 只应在少数人之间保密的。

entries.definition: Single and separate, belonging to one person.
entries.definitionCN: 单个而分开的，属于一个人的。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin adjective for what is single and cut off from the group, and every branch of meaning keeps either the belonging or the cutting.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在一个拉丁语形容词上，本义是「单个的、从群体里分出来的」，它的每一支意思都保留着「归属」或「切割」其中之一。

normal.en: Privus is Latin for single or individual, and it stands opposite publicus, the source of public.
normal.cn: privus 是拉丁语的「单个的、个人的」，与 publicus 相对，而 public 正出自后者。

normal.en: Privare means to set apart or deprive, which is why private and deprive share a stem.
normal.cn: privare 意为使分离、剥夺，所以 private 与 deprive 共用一个词干。

normal.en: Privacy adds -acy, the ending that turns an adjective into a state, as in accuracy.
normal.cn: privacy 加了 -acy，这个词尾把形容词变成状态，和 accuracy 一样。

normal.en: Private soldier was shortened to private, so the noun keeps only the rank, not the man.
normal.cn: private soldier 缩成了 private，于是这个名词只留下军衔，不再指那个人。

normal.en: In private is a fixed phrase: the preposition turns the adjective into an adverbial of manner.
normal.cn: in private 是固定说法，介词把这个形容词变成了方式状语。

abstract.en: The word carries both a belonging and a wall: something is mine because it is kept away from you.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时带着归属和一道墙：某物之所以是我的，正因为它被挡在你之外。

abstract.en: Public and private are the same coin struck twice, one face for the many and one for the one.
abstract.cn: public 与 private 是同一枚硬币的两面，一面给众人，一面给个人。

abstract.en: A private soldier is private in the oldest sense: a man serving as himself, not as an officer.
abstract.cn: 列兵的 private 用的是最老的那层意思：以本人身份服役，而不是以军官身份。

examples.en: The letters are part of his private collection.
examples.cn: 这些信件是他私人收藏的一部分。

examples.en: She moved her son from a state school to a private one.
examples.cn: 她把儿子从公立学校转到了私立学校。

examples.en: He joined up as a private and retired as a sergeant.
examples.cn: 他入伍时是列兵，退役时已是中士。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普莱维特」——「不来往」的那扇门后面，才是 private 的地方。

root: 拉丁语 privus（个人的、单独的）→ privare（使分离、剥夺）→ privatus（退离公职的、私人的）→ 古法语 privat → 中古英语 privat → private。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to one person and is therefore cut off from the rest; the senses divide into ownership, secrecy, non-state service, quiet space, and the private soldier.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「属于一个人、因而与其余部分隔开」；义项由此分出归属、保密、非国营、安静的空间，以及列兵。

core.cn: 核心意象：一扇关着的门，门后桌上摊着一封只给一个人看的信。

branches.cn: 只写着一个名字的抽屉

branches.en: a door closed before a quiet conversation
branches.cn: 悄悄谈话前关上的门

branches.en: a school with its own gate and its own fees
branches.cn: 自带大门与学费的学校

branches.cn: 别人不得进入的围墙花园

branches.en: a young soldier standing at the end of the line
branches.cn: 队列末尾站着的年轻士兵

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective for what is single and set apart, its verb of depriving, the French form, and the English endings that name the state and the manner.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「单个、被分出」的拉丁语形容词、表示剥夺的动词、法语词形，以及命名状态与方式的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin privus and privare are the secure base of this family, and privatus shows how an adjective of being set apart became the ordinary word for personal.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 privus 与 privare 是这个词族可靠的根基，privatus 则展示了一个「被分开」的形容词如何变成表示「私人」的日常词。

definition_zh: 特权；特殊待遇；荣幸；拒证权；授予特权
definition_en: a special right or advantage held by a person or group; the honour of being allowed to do something; a legal right to keep certain information secret; and, as a verb, to grant such a right

授予特权；特许

senses.title: A special right held by a person or group
senses.definition: a special right or advantage that only a particular person or group enjoys
senses.definitionCN: 只有特定的人或群体才享有的特别权利或好处
senses.example: Members of the club enjoy privileges that outsiders cannot buy.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部成员享有外人花钱也买不到的特权。
senses.why: Latin privilegium was a law aimed at one individual, so the word began as a rule made for a single person rather than for everyone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 privilegium 是专门针对某一个人立的法，所以这个词从一开始就是「为一个人单独定的规矩」，而不是对所有人通用的规矩。

senses.title: The honour of being allowed to do something
senses.definition: a special honour that comes from being given the chance to do something
senses.definitionCN: 因为获得做某事的机会而感到的一种特别的光荣
senses.example: It was a privilege to hear the old pianist play one last time.
senses.exampleCN: 能听这位老钢琴家最后一次演奏，是一种荣幸。
senses.why: If a right is granted to few people, receiving it feels like being chosen, and that feeling of being singled out is the honour sense.
senses.whyCN: 既然一项权利只授予少数人，得到它就像被选中，这种「被单独挑出来」的感受就是「荣幸」这一义。

senses.title: A legal right to keep certain information secret
senses.definition: a legal protection that lets a person or a professional refuse to reveal certain information
senses.definitionCN: 允许某个人或某种职业者拒绝透露某些信息的法律保护
senses.example: Lawyers may claim privilege over what a client tells them.
senses.exampleCN: 律师可以就当事人告知的内容主张保密特权。
senses.why: Courts borrowed the word for rights that shield a conversation from being used as evidence, keeping the old idea of a protected space.
senses.whyCN: 法庭借这个词来指「让某段谈话不被用作证据」的权利，保住的还是那个老意象：围起来的一小块受保护的空间。

senses.title: To grant someone a special right or honour
senses.definition: to give a person or group a special right, advantage, or honour that others do not have
senses.definitionCN: 给予某个人或群体一种别人没有的特别权利、好处或光荣
senses.example: The charter privileges the port city with its own customs rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这份特许状授予这座港口城市自定海关规则的权力。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by putting the thing granted in the object slot: to privilege someone is to hand them the very advantage the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词，只要把被授予的东西放进宾语位置：to privilege someone 就是把这个名词所指的那份好处交到某人手里。

intro.en: Privilege is a Roman legal term: two Latin words, one for a single person and one for law, were joined into a name for a law aimed at one case.
intro.cn: privilege 是一个罗马法术语：两个拉丁词，一个表示单个的人，一个表示法，合起来指专门针对某一例的法。

items.en: Privus meant single, individual, or set apart, and it is the element that marks the word as being about one person rather than all.
items.cn: privus 意为单个的、个人的、被分出的，正是这个词里标记「针对一个人而非所有人」的成分。

items.en: Lex meant law or statute; joined to privus it produced privilegium, a statute made for or against a named individual.
items.cn: lex 意为法律、法令；与 privus 合起来造出 privilegium，即为某个指名的人制定、或针对他的法令。

items.en: In Roman law a privilegium was an exceptional measure concerning one person, city, or group, and later the word covered any special grant or exemption.
items.cn: 在罗马法中，privilegium 是针对某一个人、城市或群体的例外措施，后来泛指任何特别的授予或豁免。

items.en: Old French took the word as privilege, meaning a right or exemption granted by an authority, and passed it into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把它写作 privilege，指权威所授予的权利或豁免，诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: English first used it for a right granted to a person, class, or town, and later added the softer sense of an honour one is glad to receive.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指授予个人、阶层或城市的权利，后来才添上「被人高看一眼、值得高兴的荣幸」这层较软的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin element privus and the English shapes built on the word; the near-meaning group gathers words for special rights and for honours.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁成分 privus 及由这个词长出的英语词形展开；近义组收表示特别权利与荣誉的词。

entries.definition: Having a special right or advantage, or having had a lucky opportunity.
entries.definitionCN: 享有特权或优势的，或有过幸运机会的。

entries.definition: Sharing a secret; it shares the Latin element privus but was built on privatus, so the formation differs.
entries.definitionCN: 参与秘密的；它同含拉丁成分 privus，却由 privatus 构成，所以构词方式不同。

entries.definition: Belonging to one person and kept from the public; it also goes back to privus through privatus.
entries.definitionCN: 属于个人、不公开的；它也经由 privatus 上溯到 privus。

entries.definition: To take something away from someone; built on the Latin verb privare, which shares the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 从某人那里拿走某物；建立在同词干的拉丁动词 privare 之上。

entries.definition: A condition that puts someone in a better position than others.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人处于比别人有利位置的条件。

entries.definition: Respect or a mark of respect that one is proud to receive.
entries.definitionCN: 值得自豪地接受的尊重或敬意。

entries.definition: A legal protection from prosecution or from a duty others must bear.
entries.definitionCN: 免于被起诉或免于承担他人义务的法律保护。

entries.definition: A right to something that a person believes they deserve.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人认为自己应得某项东西的权利。

normalIntro.en: The word joins a Latin word for single to a Latin word for law, so a privilege is literally a law written for one.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语中表示单个的词与表示法律的词拼在一起，所以 privilege 字面上就是「为一个人写的法」。

normal.en: Privus means single and lex means law, so a privilegium was a bill aimed at one named person.
normal.cn: privus 意为单个，lex 意为法律，所以 privilegium 是针对某个指名者的法案。

normal.en: The -lege in privilege is the same Latin lex that appears in legal and legislature, all of them about law.
normal.cn: privilege 里的 -lege 就是 legal、legislature 里那个拉丁语 lex，都与法律有关。

normal.en: Privileged adds -ed and turns the special right into a description of the person who holds it.
normal.cn: privileged 加 -ed 后，把特别的权利变成持有这份权利的人的描述。

normal.en: Underprivileged puts under- in front of privileged: the people who sit below the line of normal advantage.
normal.cn: underprivileged 在 privileged 前加 under-：坐在正常优势线以下的那群人。

normal.en: The legal phrase privileged information keeps the old Roman idea of a wall around certain words.
normal.cn: 法律短语 privileged information 保留的正是罗马法那个老想法：在某些话周围砌一道墙。

abstract.en: A law for one person becomes a key for a few, and the same word then names both the key and the pleasure of being handed it.
abstract.cn: 一条为一个人立的法变成一把只配给少数人的钥匙，同一个词随后既指钥匙，也指接过钥匙时的那份高兴。

abstract.en: Privilege is advantage seen from the outside; from the inside it usually feels like an honour, which is why the word can be warm and cold at once.
abstract.cn: privilege 是从外面看的优势；从里面看，它常像一份荣誉，所以这个词能同时是暖的与冷的。

abstract.en: Every privilege marks a boundary: someone is inside the wall, and the word quietly says that someone else is not.
abstract.cn: 每一项特权都标出一道界：有人站在墙内，而这个词悄悄说明另一些人不在墙内。

examples.en: Only a few readers hold the privilege of working in that locked room.
examples.cn: 只有少数读者拥有在那间上锁的书库工作的特权。

examples.en: It was a privilege to hear the old pianist play one last time.
examples.cn: 能听这位老钢琴家最后一次演奏，是一种荣幸。

examples.en: Lawyers may claim privilege over what a client tells them.
examples.cn: 律师可以就当事人告知的内容主张保密特权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普里维利己」——只让自己人占的好处，就是 privilege。

root: 拉丁语 privus（单个的、个人的）+ lex（法律）→ privilegium（针对个人的法令、特免）→ 古法语 privilege → 中古英语 privilege。同族成分 privus 还生出 private、privy、deprive 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a right reserved for few; the senses divide into the right itself, the honour of receiving it, the legal shield in court, and the act of granting it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「只留给少数人的权利」；义项分成权利本身、得到它的荣幸、法庭上的保护盾，以及授予它的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pass card handed to only a few people at the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口只发给少数人的一张通行证。

branches.en: a brass key handed across a desk
branches.cn: 桌上递过来的一枚铜钥匙

branches.en: an audience of one with a great musician
branches.cn: 只为一个人响起的大师演奏

branches.en: a lawyer closing a folder before the court
branches.cn: 律师在法庭上合上文件夹

branches.en: a charter stamped for a single port
branches.cn: 只为一座港口盖章的特许状

branches.en: the same chosen feeling, legal and personal
branches.cn: 被选中的同一种感觉，一在法度，一在人心

intro.en: The word is two Latin pieces, a word for one and a word for law, plus French and English endings; the eight entries follow the seam between them.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个拉丁成分（一个表示一，一个表示法）加上法语与英语词尾构成；下面八条沿着这道接缝展开。

latinIntro.en: Both halves of the word are attested Latin, and the compound privilegium is recorded in Roman legal texts, so the cognates here need no reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词的两半都是有记录的拉丁语词，复合形式 privilegium 见于罗马法律文本，所以这里的同族词无需重构。

items.meaning: a law for one person, a special grant

definition_zh: 概率；可能性；或然性；概率论；可信度
definition_en: the extent to which something is likely to happen or to be true, or the branch of mathematics that measures it
core_image: 一只骰子在桌上翻滚，六面朝上的机会被写成一个分数
scene: 气象员看着云图，给出明天下雨的可能性很小。The probability of rain tomorrow is low.
sceneCN: 这里指「某件事发生的可能程度」（第 2 个义项：日常可能性）；句意为明天下雨的可能性很低。可辨识物件：云图、天气图、铅笔、概率标尺。

pos.zh: 概率；可能性；或然性；概率论

senses.title: A numerical measure of chance
senses.definition: a number between zero and one expressing how likely an event is
senses.definitionCN: 取值在零与一之间、表示事件可能程度的数
senses.example: The probability of drawing an ace is one in thirteen.
senses.exampleCN: 抽到王牌的概率是十三分之一。
senses.why: Latin probabilitas named credibility; mathematics narrowed it into a number between nought and one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 probabilitas 本指可信程度；数学把它收窄成零与一之间的一个数。

senses.title: The likelihood of an event
senses.definition: how likely something is to happen, in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 日常说法里某件事发生的可能程度
senses.example: The probability of rain tomorrow is low.
senses.exampleCN: 明天下雨的可能性很低。
senses.why: The everyday sense keeps the older meaning of what may reasonably be expected.
senses.whyCN: 日常义保留较古的意思：什么可以合理地预期。

senses.title: The branch of mathematics
senses.definition: the mathematical study of chance and random events
senses.definitionCN: 研究机会与随机事件的数学分支
senses.example: Probability grew out of games of chance in the seventeenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 概率论在十七世纪从赌博游戏里发展出来。
senses.why: The name of the measure became the name of the discipline that studies it.
senses.whyCN: 这个量的名称变成了研究它的学科的名称。

senses.title: Conditional probability
senses.definition: the chance of one event given that another event has occurred
senses.definitionCN: 在另一事件已发生的前提下，某一事件发生的可能
senses.example: Conditional probability changes when the first event is known.
senses.exampleCN: 已知第一个事件之后，条件概率就改变了。
senses.why: Knowledge of one event removes part of the sample space, so the measure is recalculated within what remains.
senses.whyCN: 知道一个事件发生会去掉部分样本空间，于是概率在剩下的范围里重算。

senses.title: A value used in significance testing
senses.definition: the chance of seeing data at least this extreme if the null hypothesis holds
senses.definitionCN: 在原假设成立时，看到至少这样极端的数据的机会
senses.example: A probability below the threshold led the team to reject the null hypothesis.
senses.exampleCN: 概率低于阈值，使研究团队否定了原假设。
senses.why: Testing turns probability into a decision rule: if the chance of the data is small, the assumption is doubted.
senses.whyCN: 检验把概率变成一条决策规则：若数据出现的机会很小，就怀疑那个前提。

senses.title: The phrase 'in all probability'
senses.definition: a fixed phrase meaning that something is almost certain
senses.definitionCN: 一个表示某事几乎确定的固定说法
senses.example: In all probability, the train will be late.
senses.exampleCN: 十有八九，这趟车会晚点。
senses.why: The phrase adds 'all' to the measure in order to say that the likelihood is very high.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法在概率前加「全部」，以表示可能程度非常高。

senses.title: A very small chance
senses.definition: a chance so small that it is worth naming as remote
senses.definitionCN: 小到值得称为「渺茫」的机会
senses.example: There is a probability, though a remote one, that the letter was lost.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信有可能丢失，尽管机会渺茫。
senses.why: English can use the same noun for a low value as for a high one, with a qualifier to mark the scale.
senses.whyCN: 英语可以用同一个名词指低值，也可以指高值，只靠限定词标出高低。

senses.title: Credibility of a statement
senses.definition: the degree to which an account or a claim deserves belief
senses.definitionCN: 一种说法或主张值得相信的程度
senses.example: The probability of her account rests on two witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 她的说法有多可信，取决于两位证人。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is exactly this: what is worthy of approval, before any number is attached.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层正是如此：什么值得认可，还没有附上任何数字。

intro.en: Probability comes from Latin probabilitas 'credibility', from probabilis 'that can be approved or proved', from probare 'to test, prove'. It reached English through Old French in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: probability 出自拉丁 probabilitas「可信」，再上溯形容词 probabilis「可认可、可证明的」，动词为 probare「检验、证明」；十四世纪经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Probare meant 'to test, examine, prove'. It is related to probus 'good, upright', and the pair belongs to an old root of testing and approval, reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: probare 意为「检验、审查、证明」。它与 probus「好、正直」相关，这一对词属于一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根为重构形式，并无直接书证。

items.en: Probus meant 'good, honest, upright', said of people and of quality. The link with probare is generally accepted, though the exact root shape is reconstructed.
items.cn: probus 意为「好、诚实、正直」，可用于人和品质。它与 probare 的联系一般被接受，但确切词根形态属重构。

items.en: Probabilis meant 'that can be approved, credible', and was used of opinions and evidence before it was used of numbers.
items.cn: probabilis 意为「可认可的、可信的」，先用于意见与证据，后用于数字。

items.en: The abstract noun probabilitas named the quality of being credible, the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 抽象名词 probabilitas 指可信的性质，是英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French probabilite carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of likelihood or plausibility.
items.cn: 古法语 probabilite 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指「看似可能」。

items.en: The numerical sense developed with the mathematics of games of chance in the seventeenth century, and the discipline took the word as its name.
items.cn: 数值义随十七世纪赌博数学发展起来，这门学科也把这个词当作名称。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same proving root that are easy to confuse; group two holds words for how likely something is.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「检验、证明」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示「有多大可能」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something likely or credible; the noun is its abstract form.
entries.definitionCN: 表示很可能或可信的形容词；名词是它的抽象形式。

entries.definition: Able to be demonstrated by evidence; it comes from prove, which shares the Latin proving root.
entries.definitionCN: 可由证据证明的；出自与拉丁「证明」同根的 prove。

entries.definition: Evidence that settles a question; the noun of result from the same proving root.
entries.definitionCN: 能定论一个问题的证据；同根的结果名词。

entries.definition: Uprightness of character, from probus 'good'; it looks like probability but names a virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 品行的正直，出自 probus「好」；形似 probability，却指一种德性。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for the chance of something, with no mathematical claim.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事机会的日常名词，不带数学含义。

entries.definition: The possibility that something happens, often spoken informally.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能，常用于口语。

entries.definition: The ratio between the chances of two outcomes, as in betting.
entries.definitionCN: 两种结果机会之比，常用于博彩。

entries.definition: Something that can happen, with no statement about how often.
entries.definitionCN: 可能发生的事，不说明频率。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'test and approve', so probability began as credibility and only later became a number.
normal.cn: 词根意为「检验与认可」，因此概率最初指可信，后来才变成数字。

normal.en: One family runs probability, probable, probably, probabilistic, improbable and probity.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：概率、很可能的、很可能、概率的、不太可能的、正直。

normal.en: The same proving root gives proof, prove and provable, all about evidence rather than chance.
normal.cn: 同一「证明」词根还给出证据、证明、可证明的，都关于证据而非机会。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: the probability of, in all probability, conditional probability.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：某事的概率、十有八九、条件概率。

normal.en: A probability is a number between nought and one; anything outside that range is not a probability at all.
normal.cn: 概率是零与一之间的数；超出这个范围的就不是概率。

abstract.en: Picture a die rolling across a table, with one face counted and written as a fraction.
abstract.cn: 想象一只骰子在桌上翻滚，某一面被数出来写成一个分数。

abstract.en: Picture a weather map with a shaded band whose width shows how unsure the forecaster is.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图，上面一条带阴影的宽带显示预报员有多不确定。

abstract.en: Picture a jury weighing two witnesses, deciding how much credit a story deserves.
abstract.cn: 想象陪审团权衡两位证人，判断一个说法值多少信任。

examples.en: The probability of two heads in a row is one quarter.
examples.cn: 连续两次抛出正面的概率是四分之一。

examples.en: In all probability the meeting will end early.
examples.cn: 十有八九，会议会提前结束。

examples.en: Conditional probability depends on what is already known.
examples.cn: 条件概率取决于已知的情况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「检验、证明」，加抽象名词词尾表示「可被认可的性质」：先指说法可信，后指数值化的机会大小。

root: 拉丁 probabilitas「可信」＝ probabilis「可认可的」＋抽象名词词尾，probabilis 出自 probare「检验、证明」，与 probus「正直」同属一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根为重构形式。英语十四世纪经古法语传入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: something is weighed and found more or less worthy of belief. That weighing becomes a number, then a discipline, then a decision rule, and finally any estimate of how likely a claim is to be true.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个观念展开：把某事放在天平上称一称，看它值多少信任。这种称量先变成数字，再变成学科，再变成决策规则，最后指对一种说法为真的可能程度的估计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a die rolling across a table while a shaded band on a weather map shows how unsure the answer is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只骰子在桌上翻滚，同时天气图上一条阴影带显示答案有多不确定。

branches.en: A NUMBER: the technical value and the everyday likelihood are one scale, read precisely or loosely.
branches.cn: 一个数：技术数值与日常可能程度是同一把尺，只是读得精或粗。

branches.en: A DISCIPLINE: the study of chance, including the case where part of the answer is already known.
branches.cn: 一门学科：研究机会，包括已知部分答案的情形。

branches.en: TEST RULE: a small probability of the data becomes grounds for doubting an assumption.
branches.cn: 检验规则：数据出现机会很小，就成了怀疑某个前提的理由。

branches.en: SCALE: the same noun can name a near certainty or a remote chance, with a qualifier to mark which end.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一个名词既可指近乎确定，也可指渺茫机会，靠限定词标出哪一端。

branches.en: CREDIBILITY: the oldest layer asks how much belief a statement deserves.
branches.cn: 可信度：最古老的一层问的是一种说法值多少相信。

intro.en: Probability is a Latin abstract noun from a verb of testing; the same root builds the adjectives and the plain verb for proving.
intro.cn: probability 是一个拉丁抽象名词，出自表示检验的动词；同一词根还构成形容词与表示证明的普通动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare gives probabilitas, probabilis and probus; the English family includes probable, proof, prove and probity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 probare 衍生 probabilitas、probabilis 与 probus；英语词族包括 probable、proof、prove、probity。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of testing something before believing it.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「先检验再相信」的意思。

items.example: The adjective adds a moral shade to the same root.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给同一词根加上道德色彩。

items.meaning: able to be approved or proved
items.example: The adjective names what passes the test.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指能通过检验的东西。

items.example: The noun names the quality, then the measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指性质，后指度量。

definition_zh: 很可能的；可信的；有理由的；有相当根据的
definition_en: likely to happen or to be true, or reasonable enough to be believed
core_image: 天平两端各放一份证据，装证据较多的一侧缓缓下沉
scene: 气象员指着西边压来的云层，判断傍晚前会有雷暴。A storm is probable by evening.
sceneCN: 这里指「很可能会发生的」（第 1 个义项：事件很可能发生）；句意为傍晚之前很可能有一场雷暴。可辨识物件：云层、风向标、雷达图、记录板；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 很可能的；可信的；有理由的

senses.title: Likely to happen
senses.definition: having a strong chance of happening
senses.definitionCN: 发生的可能性很大
senses.example: A storm is probable by evening.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚之前很可能有一场雷暴。
senses.why: The Latin adjective means 'that can be approved', and what can be approved is what the evidence supports.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词意为「可获认可的」，而可获认可的就是证据所支持的东西。

senses.title: Credible as an account
senses.definition: likely to be true, said of a story or an explanation
senses.definitionCN: 很可能为真，用于说法或解释
senses.example: Her version of events is probable, though not proved.
senses.exampleCN: 她对事情的描述很可信，尽管未获证明。
senses.why: The oldest sense concerns belief rather than events: a probable account is one worthy of acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项关乎相信而非事件：可信的说法就是值得接受的说法。

senses.title: Supported by reasoning
senses.definition: resting on reasons that make it sensible to accept
senses.definitionCN: 有理由支撑，使接受它显得合理
senses.example: The simplest probable explanation is often the right one.
senses.exampleCN: 最简单的、说得通的解释往往就是对的。
senses.why: A conclusion is probable when the reasons for it outweigh the reasons against, a weighing rather than a proof.
senses.whyCN: 当支持的理由重于反对的理由，结论就是「说得通」的；这是称量，而非证明。

senses.title: Reasonable grounds in law
senses.definition: having enough evidence for an officer to act, in the fixed phrase probable cause
senses.definitionCN: 证据足以让执法人员采取行动，用于固定说法「合理根据」
senses.example: The search was allowed because there was probable cause.
senses.exampleCN: 由于存在合理根据，这次搜查获得准许。
senses.why: Law borrows the weighing image and asks whether the evidence is strong enough to justify action, not to convict.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用了称量的形象，问的是证据是否足以支持行动，而不是足以定罪。

senses.title: Likely in a scientific estimate
senses.titleCN: 科学估计中的或然结论
senses.definition: likely according to a model or an estimate rather than a certainty
senses.definitionCN: 依模型或估计而言很可能，而非确定
senses.example: The probable range of the signal was published with the data.
senses.exampleCN: 信号的或然范围随数据一并发表。
senses.why: Science states results as probable ranges, keeping the word's sense of what the evidence supports.
senses.whyCN: 科学把结果说成或然范围，保留了「证据所支持」的意思。

senses.title: The expected winner
senses.definition: the competitor expected to win, in the phrase the probable winner
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法中指被预期会赢的参赛者
senses.example: She was the probable winner before the final heat.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后一轮预赛之前，她是最被看好的人。
senses.why: Expectation based on evidence is the same weighing applied to a field of competitors.
senses.whyCN: 基于证据的预期，就是同一种称量用在参赛者身上。

senses.title: A probable opinion in moral theology
senses.definition: an opinion with solid support that may be followed without certainty, in the older theological use
senses.definitionCN: 有可靠依据、无需确定即可采纳的意见，属较早的神学用法
senses.example: The older manuals asked whether a probable opinion could safely be followed.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的手册会问：一个可采意见是否能被安全遵循。
senses.why: This technical sense keeps the Latin meaning exactly: an opinion that can be approved, even without proof.
senses.whyCN: 这个专门义精确保留拉丁原义：一种即使未获证明也可获认可的意见。

senses.title: Belief made reasonable by evidence
senses.titleCN: 抽象：证据使相信成为合理
senses.definition: the quality of a claim whose evidence makes belief reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 一种主张因证据而使相信显得合理的性质
senses.example: What makes the claim probable is not certainty but the weight of the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 使这个主张可信的不是确定性，而是证据的分量。
senses.why: The abstract sense isolates the weighing itself, without naming an event, an account or a court.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把称量本身单独提出来，不指事件、说法或法庭。

intro.en: Probable comes through Old French from Latin probabilis 'that can be approved or proved', an adjective from probare 'to test, prove'. It entered English in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: probable 经古法语来自拉丁形容词 probabilis「可认可、可证明的」，出自动词 probare「检验、证明」；十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: Probare meant 'to test, examine, prove'. It belongs with probus 'good, upright' to an old root of testing and approval; that root is reconstructed.
items.cn: probare 意为「检验、审查、证明」。它与 probus「好、正直」同属一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根属重构形式。

items.en: Probabilis meant 'that can be approved, credible'. It described opinions and evidence long before it described events.
items.cn: probabilis 意为「可获认可的、可信的」，在用于事件之前，长期用于意见与证据。

items.en: Old French probable passed the adjective into English in the fourteenth century, where it first meant credible rather than likely to happen.
items.cn: 古法语 probable 在十四世纪把这个形容词带入英语，最初意为「可信」，而非「很可能发生」。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word was increasingly used of future events, so likelihood joined credibility.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词越来越多用于未来事件，于是「可能发生」与「可信」合并。

items.en: The legal phrase probable cause is a fixed term of art, and its earliest uses are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 法律短语「合理根据」是一个固定术语，其最早用例只能给出约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same proving root that are easily confused; group two holds words for what is likely or believable.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「证明」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示「很可能」或「可信」的词。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for likelihood or credibility; the adjective is its descriptive form.
entries.definitionCN: 表示可能性或可信的抽象名词；形容词是它的描述形式。

entries.definition: Able to be demonstrated; it comes from prove, which shares the Latin proving root but stresses demonstration.
entries.definitionCN: 可被证明的；出自 prove，同享拉丁「证明」词根，但强调实证。

entries.definition: Tending to prove something, used of evidence in law.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于证明某事的，用于法律上的证据。

entries.definition: From plaudere 'to applaud': originally 'deserving applause', hence seemingly reasonable; it is not the proving root.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 plaudere「鼓掌」，原意「值得鼓掌」，引申为「看似有理」；与「证明」词根无关。

entries.definition: The everyday adjective for a strong chance, without the evidential weight that probable carries.
entries.definitionCN: 表示机会很大的日常形容词，不带 probable 那种证据分量。

entries.definition: From credere 'to believe': able to be believed, close to the older sense of probable.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 credere「相信」，意为「可被相信」，接近 probable 较古的义项。

entries.definition: Able to be accepted as true, often said of stories and excuses.
entries.definitionCN: 能被当作真实接受的，常用于说法与借口。

entries.definition: Anticipated as likely to occur, with less emphasis on evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 预期会发生，对证据的强调较少。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'test and approve', so probable first meant believable and only later meant likely to happen.
normal.cn: 词根意为「检验与认可」，因此 probable 先指可信，后来才指很可能发生。

normal.en: One family runs probable, probably, probability, probabilistic, improbable and probity.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：很可能的、很可能、概率、概率的、不太可能的、正直。

normal.en: The legal phrase probable cause is a fixed term, not a free combination.
normal.cn: 法律短语「合理根据」是固定术语，不是可以随意组合的说法。

normal.en: Other words about proof are close relatives: prove, proof, provable, probative.
normal.cn: 其他关于证明的词是近亲：证明、证据、可证明的、有证明力的。

normal.en: Plausible looks like a relative but comes from applause, not from proof.
normal.cn: plausible 看似同族，实际出自「鼓掌」，与「证明」无关。

abstract.en: Picture two pans of evidence on a balance, the heavier one slowly winning.
abstract.cn: 想象天平两端各放一份证据，较重的一侧缓缓占上风。

abstract.en: Picture a witness whose story holds together under every question.
abstract.cn: 想象一位证人的说法在每一次追问下都站得住。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where the standard is enough evidence to act, not enough to convict.
abstract.cn: 想象一个法庭，标准是「足以行动的证据」，而非「足以定罪」。

examples.en: It is probable that the flight will be delayed.
examples.cn: 这趟航班很可能会延误。

examples.en: The police must show probable cause before a search.
examples.cn: 警方在搜查之前必须说明合理根据。

examples.en: The theory is probable but not yet proved.
examples.cn: 这个理论说得通，但尚未获得证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「检验、证明」，加形容词词尾表示「能被……的」：能被检验通过的，先是「可信」，后是「很可能」。

root: 拉丁 probabilis「可认可的」＝ probare「检验、证明」＋形容词词尾 -abilis，与 probus「正直」同属一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根属重构形式。英语十四世纪经古法语传入，最初意为「可信」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: evidence is weighed. When the heavier side carries belief, a statement is credible; when it carries expectation, an event is likely; law and science fix the threshold of action and of conclusion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把证据放到天平上称。较重的一侧支撑相信时，说法就可信；支撑预期时，事件就很可能；法律与科学则各自定出行动与结论的门槛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pans of evidence on a balance, the heavier one slowly winning.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端各放着一份证据，较重的一侧缓缓占上风。

branches.en: WEIGH: likelihood and credibility are the same balance read toward the future or the past.
branches.cn: 称量：可能发生与可信，是天平朝未来或朝过去读的两个方向。

branches.en: REASON ENOUGH: when reasons outweigh counter-reasons, the conclusion is probable.
branches.cn: 理由足够：当支持的理由重于反对的理由，结论就是说得通的。

branches.en: THE BAR: the law asks only whether there is enough for action.
branches.cn: 门槛：法律只问证据是否足以行动。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE: science and older moral theology both fix what may be held without certainty.
branches.cn: 专门领域：科学与较早的道德神学都定出「无确定也可持有」的范围。

branches.en: EXPECTATION: evidence can also pick a likely winner, or simply make belief reasonable.
branches.cn: 预期：证据也能挑出被看好的人，或只是使相信显得合理。
